questions.q: Where does the New Year’s message say all change begins?
options: With better luck
Not quite. The article says: Within oneself – “God does not change the condition of a people until they change themselves”.
Within oneself – “God does not change the condition of a people until they change themselves”
Yes. The new year as a project of inner renewal.
With other people’s behaviour
Not quite. The article says: Within oneself – “God does not change the condition of a people until they change themselves”.
With a change of government
Not quite. The article says: Within oneself – “God does not change the condition of a people until they change themselves”.
questions.rationale: “Make the new year a project of inner renewal. All change begins within.”

questions.article: A Tragic Day in Delhi and Call for Peace
questions.q: After the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, a man acted in a way that could have reignited conflict. How did the Prophet respond?
options: He rewarded him
Not quite. The article says: He refused to support or shelter him, calling him a kindler of war.
He refused to support or shelter him, calling him a kindler of war
Right. There is no place for those who disrupt the peace of society.
He ignored the matter
Not quite. The article says: He refused to support or shelter him, calling him a kindler of war.
He ended the treaty
Not quite. The article says: He refused to support or shelter him, calling him a kindler of war.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet refused to support him or allow him refuge in Madinah, stating that such a person was a kindler of war.”

questions.article: A Tragic Day in Delhi and Call for Peace
questions.q: Why does the article ask every family to examine the atmosphere of its home?
options: Children should not hear the news
Not quite. The article says: Words of hate spoken at home take root in young minds; peace in the world begins with peace at home.
Homes are where most accidents occur
Not quite. The article says: Words of hate spoken at home take root in young minds; peace in the world begins with peace at home.
Families should avoid their neighbours
Not quite. The article says: Words of hate spoken at home take root in young minds; peace in the world begins with peace at home.
Words of hate spoken at home take root in young minds; peace in the world begins with peace at home
Yes. A home should be “a cradle of peace.”
questions.rationale: “When parents speak the language of hate, their words take root in young, impressionable minds… Peace in the world can only begin with peace at home.”

questions.q: What does the article call the actual spirit of fasting, beyond abstaining from food and drink?
options: Sleeping through the day
Not quite. The article says: Refraining from negative thinking and negative language – following reason over desire.
Refraining from negative thinking and negative language – following reason over desire
Well read. If abused, one says only “I am fasting.”
Eating less through the year
Not quite. The article says: Refraining from negative thinking and negative language – following reason over desire.
Avoiding other people
Not quite. The article says: Refraining from negative thinking and negative language – following reason over desire.
questions.rationale: “The actual spirit of fasting is to refrain from indulging in negative thinking and the use of negative language.”

questions.q: Which is the first of the two principles the author put before a gathering of youth for the country’s progress?
options: Placing personal interest first
Not quite. The article says: Placing national interest above personal interest.
Placing national interest above personal interest
Correct. Giving to the nation, not only taking from it.
Avoiding people of other communities
Not quite. The article says: Placing national interest above personal interest.
Waiting for the government to act
Not quite. The article says: Placing national interest above personal interest.
questions.rationale: “The first principle is that national interest must be placed above personal interest.”

questions.article: Planting the Tree of the Nation
questions.q: Told that a tree would take a hundred years to mature, the reply was “plant it this afternoon.” What does the article apply this to?
options: The need to wait for better times
Not quite. The article says: Nation-building – a long task that needs patient, steady work begun at once, not slogans.
Nation-building – a long task that needs patient, steady work begun at once, not slogans
Yes. “Noise cannot produce growth.”
Gardening as a hobby
Not quite. The article says: Nation-building – a long task that needs patient, steady work begun at once, not slogans.
Quick political victories
Not quite. The article says: Nation-building – a long task that needs patient, steady work begun at once, not slogans.
questions.rationale: “If it will take a century, then we must begin immediately and plant our ‘tree’ without delay.”

questions.q: What does the article say one should do on meeting unkindness from others?
options: Break off all dealings
Not quite. The article says: Not return it, but go on behaving with sympathy.
Not return it, but go on behaving with sympathy
Right. “God will be merciful to those who are merciful.”
Return it in equal measure
Not quite. The article says: Not return it, but go on behaving with sympathy.
Complain to others
Not quite. The article says: Not return it, but go on behaving with sympathy.
questions.rationale: “Even when one experiences unkindness from others one should not return unkindness for unkindness, but should continue to behave sympathetically.”

questions.q: A king asked the envoys of a later court, “Where are those men who used to come before?” – men in palm-fibre sandals. What does the article conclude?
options: Kings prefer familiar faces
Not quite. The article says: True strength lies in inner capability and moral resolve, not in luxury or display.
Fine clothes win respect
Not quite. The article says: True strength lies in inner capability and moral resolve, not in luxury or display.
True strength lies in inner capability and moral resolve, not in luxury or display
Yes. Those with few needs decide freely and sacrifice readily.
Poor envoys make better bargains
Not quite. The article says: True strength lies in inner capability and moral resolve, not in luxury or display.
questions.rationale: “True strength does not lie in luxury, ornamentation, or authority, but in inner capability and moral resolve.”

questions.q: What does the article name as the key that activates the mind’s power of resilience?
options: Immediate reaction
Not quite. The article says: Patience – pausing in silence so the mind can settle and repair itself.
Patience – pausing in silence so the mind can settle and repair itself
Exactly. “Indeed, God is with the patient.”
Keeping busy without pause
Not quite. The article says: Patience – pausing in silence so the mind can settle and repair itself.
Talking the matter over at length
Not quite. The article says: Patience – pausing in silence so the mind can settle and repair itself.
questions.rationale: “The key to activating this power is an eight-letter mantra: patience… Through patience, we enable this inner repair mechanism to function.”

questions.q: Where does the article say wealth belongs?
options: With one’s heirs alone
Not quite. The article says: In the hand, not in the heart – a means for one’s needs, not life’s purpose.
In the heart, as life’s chief aim
Not quite. The article says: In the hand, not in the heart – a means for one’s needs, not life’s purpose.
Nowhere – it should be rejected
Not quite. The article says: In the hand, not in the heart – a means for one’s needs, not life’s purpose.
In the hand, not in the heart – a means for one’s needs, not life’s purpose
Well reasoned. Knowledge is the higher wealth.
questions.rationale: “The wise approach is not to reject wealth but to place it where it belongs: in the hand, not in the heart.”
